name: Chalet Hotels Ltd
title: Chalet Hotels Ltd - 542399 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Chalet Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR5,711 million and EBITDA 8% to INR2,786 million, while hospitality RevPAR fell 3% on Mumbai weakness.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was uneven: a soft January in Mumbai and a March slump from West Asia tensions cut foreign-tourist room nights (about 9,000 lost in March alone), with management putting the disruption at 10-12% of business. Hospitality revenue grew 3% to INR4,740 million and EBITDA 1% to INR2,248 million, with margin down 102 bps to 47.4%. Ex-residential revenue grew 6% to INR5,706 million with a 49.1% EBITDA margin. Management guided to a strong recovery in the second half and planned about INR30 billion of capex over FY27-FY29, mainly from internal accruals, while adding the Udaipur resort and a 330-key Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,740 million (+3%) and EBITDA INR2,248 million (+1%); Mumbai underperformed while South hotels and resorts (Westin Rishikesh) did well. Resort occupancy averaged about 43% for FY26, targeted to trend toward 60%.

segments.name: Commercial real estate
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,061 million (+55%) at an 83.1% EBITDA margin. March 2026 monthly rental run-rate INR280 million; committed occupancy about 88%, with Bangalore above 83% (management later cited about 91%) and Powai at 90%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Phase 1 has 152 units handed over and one pending. Phase 2 (168 units) is due for handover in FY27, plus 160,000 sq ft of commercial space yet to be developed.

guidance_outlook: Monthly CRE rentals expected to scale to about INR300 million during FY27; CIGNUS II commissioning in FY28 to drive a step change.
Planned capex of about INR30 billion over FY27-FY29 covering hospitality and CRE, including announced acquisitions, expected to be funded through internal accruals.
Enabling approval for debt raise of up to INR10 billion; management said there is no immediate plan to raise incremental debt.
Management expects a strong recovery and bounce-back in the second half of FY27 as marriages return from the Middle East to India.
Management expects Q1 FY27 to be fairly strong, with April stronger than expected, May strong against a weak base, and June steady.
Management expects leisure portfolio EBITDA margins to reach at least the mid-40s; city hotel margins expected to remain stable rather than expand.
Management expects RevPAR growth in the mid to high single digits to translate into mid-to-high double-digit room revenue growth for FY27 (answered 'Yes').
capex_capacity: Operating keys 3,389 with about 1,655 pipeline keys across 7 assets, taking total to over 5,000 keys.
Udaipur resort acquired for INR1,710 million (144 keys on 8.2 acres); upgrade to upper-upscale planned, with timelines, capex and brand not yet disclosed.

Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad: 330-key ultra-luxury hotel outside Mindspace Madhapur on a warm-shell lease from Mindspace REIT; pure construction capex INR5,600 million (INR560 crore) including 40,000 sq ft commercial space, fit-out largely after possession in Q4 FY28; launch by end FY29.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for substantial completion by end FY27, though West Asia has pressured labour availability.
Taj project at Delhi International Airport: 70 rooms to launch by Q4 FY27, balance inventory in phases.
Bangalore added 129 rooms (management also cited 121 rooms in Q&A); Athiva Khandala had its first full quarter at full inventory, with ADR north of INR15,000.
Capital WIP and assets not yielding returns at INR8.3 billion at year-end (management split: IPUC about INR486 crore, CWIP INR132 crore, inventory about INR269 crore).
demand_pricing: Mumbai ADR growth of 0-2% and occupancy down 0-2 pp in Jan-Mar 2026 per industry reports, versus India ADR growth of 6-8%; the Powai property was also hit by CIGNUS II construction.
February was very strong, with some South hotels up over 35% YoY; March cancellations cost about 9,000 foreign-tourist room nights, and management put total disruption at 10-12%.
Management said domestic traveller demand showed no meaningful decline; the group/MICE share rose from 20% to 22% of business in the last month.
Management reiterated that Athiva ADR is north of INR15,000 and expects Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad ADR around INR25,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why use a subsidiary-level minority dilution at DIAL rather than debt or internal funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a one-time project-level minority partnership, not a capital decision; the balance sheet is strong and no fundraising is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-FY29 capex funding mix and peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Khanna said the entire INR30 billion for announced projects will be funded through internal accruals, with no major borrowing unless a strategic acquisition arises.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CRE leasing taking until FY28 to fully let out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the leasing comment applied to CIGNUS II; existing inventory is above 90% occupied, so only about 10% remains to lease there.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hyderabad capex and pricing assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is INR560 crore construction cost (INR630 crore earlier included IDC and lease deposit); management expects ADR around INR25,000 but declined to give stabilisation timing or lease terms.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the INR800 crore of capital WIP sit on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Khanna said about INR486 crore is in IPUC, INR132 crore in CWIP and about INR269 crore in inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: City hotel margins are at a stable point and will not expand much; leisure margins can rise to the mid-40s, CRE margins are at 83-84%, and Bangalore ramp-up will matter.

risks_watch: West Asia tensions and continuing foreign-tourist cancellations, with management saying April was stronger but June only steady.
Mumbai softness and Powai disruption from CIGNUS II construction (banquet connectivity and crew attrition), with closure expected next quarter.
Bangalore 129-room addition still ramping; occupancy must move toward 60% to support margins.
Capex of INR30 billion over FY27-FY29 and the INR10 billion enabling debt approval; watch leverage despite the stated internal funding.
Labour availability at CIGNUS II and the timing of Hyderabad and Udaipur project disclosures, which management has not yet provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story and the H2 recovery, but defensive and at times evasive on Mumbai weakness, peer RevPAR gaps and project-level guidance. Management declined to give Udaipur timelines and capex and Hyderabad stabilisation details.
key_quotes: Overall, I think the political tensions have caused about a 10% to 12% disruption in our business.
So, for announced projects, this entire INR30 billion will be funded through internal accruals.
We are trying out a project level partnership that we have not tried before.
Our existing inventory is above 90% occupancy right now.

growth.why: Management guides mid-to-high double-digit room revenue growth for FY27 on mid-to-high single-digit RevPAR growth, backed by a strong H2 recovery expected as marriages return, April/May trends, and capacity adds (Taj Delhi 70 rooms by Q4 FY27, CIGNUS II by end FY27, Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad by FY29), though the recovery case is largely qualitative and the Q4 hospitality disruption was 10-12%.
